setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Of course, you already had a conversation with Kim.

prospect.name: Frank Somma
prospect.family_status: Has a son who turns eight in February
prospect.training_background: Played sports in high school; used personal trainers on and off since the early 2000s, none in the last 2-3 years. Currently training 5+ days/week, machines and light free weights, single muscle groups, 1.5-2 hour sessions plus incline power walking. Down from 235 lb in January to 217 lb.
prospect.medical: L4/L5 disc herniation from car accidents and a slip-and-fall; knee issues; active right shoulder problem with clicking and bone-on-bone rubbing, in pain for the past month, cannot do overhead work (physical therapist and chiropractor both saw it and found no structural rotator cuff damage); history of cancer, described as 'gone now'; Lyme disease; heavy metal toxicity; toxic mold; autoimmune issues and autoimmune fatigue; repeated hospitalisations since his son was born. Currently seeing a chiropractor once or twice a week and considering starting with a physical therapist.

signals: Lost years to cancer, Lyme, mould and autoimmune illness and is now rebuilding: 'I went through cancer for a few years, which is gone now, luckily'
Explicit regret about what illness cost him as a father: 'he's never seen me really healthy. I've been kind of like in and out of the hospital since he was born'
Wants a former self back rather than good-to-great: 'I kind of remember what I used to look normal in'
Not the_prehab_fighter: the cancer is described as resolved, not active

goals.text: Get under 200 lb, ideally 185-195, losing roughly another 20 lb
Improve mobility and agility rather than build bulk; stop losing range of motion whenever he strength-trains
Train with compound, full-body kettlebell movements instead of isolated machine work, and do it without re-injuring himself
Have consistent energy through the day instead of autoimmune fatigue and needing to sleep
Be a physically capable role model his son can look at and keep up with
Know he could take on something very challenging - a Tough Mudder or Spartan-type event - if he chose to, and jog again without fear
Lock in a foundation now so he does not have a painful old age or depend on others when older
Get back into smaller clothes - a medium shirt and a 30-32 waist rather than a 34-36

pains.text: L4/L5 disc herniation and knee issues from car accidents and a fall; fears one bad rep sets him back weeks
Active right shoulder problem - clicking, bone-on-bone rubbing, painful for the past month even without training; cannot do overhead pressing
History of cancer, Lyme disease, heavy metal toxicity, toxic mould and autoimmune illness leaving him prone to inflammation and fatigue
Plateaued after three months of hard effort - scale not moving despite training up to twice a day
No structured or targeted plan; piecing it together from YouTube and 'flying blind'
Previous trainers, including some with medical backgrounds, did not understand the complexity of his condition and overestimated what he could do
Knows from history that he relapses - 'I've been in incredibly good shape in periods of my life and then I've gone backwards'
Spending 1.5-2 hours per session with diminishing returns, which makes him want to quit
Missed years of his son's life - had to say no to hikes, trips and amusement parks

objections.raw_quote: But I know with pedal bells, there's a lot of pressing. There's a lot of overhead pressing. So I may need to, you know, go a little bit easy on that side, possibly, maybe just go super light.
objections.rep_response: Agreed it was normal to start light and said they would make sure his form was correct; did not ask whether his physical therapist or chiropractor had cleared overhead loading.

objections.raw_quote: if I'm going to work with anybody, it has to be something that like, can't just either do myself at the gym or find on YouTube
objections.rep_response: Asked what made him book the call rather than keep figuring it out alone, then reframed his need as wanting something bespoke rather than cookie-cutter.

objections.raw_quote: I mean, I don't, I don't know this person. don't know what their relationship is going to be like, and I can't say that, you know, 100% and, you know, invest in it.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged he would have to experience it, then asked him to answer on gut feeling instead; got 'I'm interested'.

objections.raw_quote: Okay. Yeah, I'll think about it. I'm actually, I'm investigating a couple of other opportunities right now. So I have to, you know, I have to meet with this trainer. I've got another person from the internet that I'm meeting with this week also.
objections.rep_response: Asked whether the hesitation was the offer itself or only the comparison to other options, then started to probe his decision checklist; the prospect cut it off saying he had to go.

objections.raw_quote: I get off of this call really soon, because I have another meeting coming up, so if you could kind of get to that point, that would be helpful.
objections.rep_response: Said 'we're almost there' and pressed one more commitment question before quoting the price.

evidence: Prospect explicitly deferred: 'Yeah, I'll think about it.'
He is actively shopping: 'I have to meet with this trainer. I've got another person from the internet that I'm meeting with this week also.'
Counter-evidence for a warmer read: 'it sounds like it could be a good fit for me' and 'I'm interested.'
Counter-evidence for a colder read: he ended the call abruptly - 'we're kind of talking about the same things over and over again, and I don't mean to be rude, but, like, I got the information'
No payment link was sent, no payment taken, and no follow-up date was agreed
outcome.next_step: Prospect said he would get back to the rep after meeting two other coaching options; no date or link agreed.

notable.note: Extensive and serious medical history - resolved cancer, Lyme, autoimmune disease, L4/L5 herniation and an actively painful right shoulder that his PT and chiropractor have been treating - and the rep never asked whether any clinician had cleared him for loaded kettlebell work. The offer was presented at 00:47 with only two minutes of call left because the prospect had a hard stop, so the price landed with no time for a proper close, and the rep's answer to 'what's the breakdown of that over six months' was vague ('he jumps on whenever it's needed').

quality.notes: Severe and persistent. Whole passages are inverted - the rep's opening frame and the scripted opener 'Tell me, what can we potentially specifically help you with, Frank?' are both attributed to Frank Somma, and long stretches from 00:07 to 00:09 and 00:42 to 00:43 alternate wrongly. Role was read from content throughout.
